docs.title: Welcome to Hokuyo UST Documentation
docs.text: this pages we will talk about configuring two lidar and install it in paralel

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• ROS Noetic installed
  • Ubuntu 20.04 LTS
  • HOKUYO UST-10LX

after everything ready, lets jump into step by step

docs.title: Operating Hokuyo UST-10LX
docs.text: there is two way to operating the LIDAR. the first one is by using Ethernet and the second one is via USB Cables. but in this section, we just covering connetion via Ethernet.

docs.title: Plug your Ethernet!
docs.text: first of all you need to connect your LIDAR Ethernet Cables into your peripheral Ethernet Ports. its an easy task to do.

docs.title: Power up your LIDAR
docs.text: in order to run and communicate via Ethernet cables, you need to give LIDAR with 12 Volt to 24 Volt DC Supply.

docs.title: Configuring Ethernet
docs.text:
the default IP Address for Hokuyo UST-10LX is 192.168.0.10. we need to connect to that IP Address in order to communicate. we can run this following command:

sudo ip addr add 192.168.0.1/24 dev eth0

after that make sure that IP Address is available in your eth0 interface using this commands:

ifconfig

or

ip -a

it will show the Hokuyo UST-10LX IP Address

docs.title: Run ROS
docs.text: you need 3 separate terminal to run LIDAR via ROS.

docs.title: Terminal 1
docs.text:
we will run roscore in this terminal, but you need the prerequisite things to do.

source /opt/ros/noetic/setup.bash

move to your catkin workspace directory catkin_ws and run following command:

source devel/setup.bash

after sourcing the setup.bash in ROS and Catkin, we will run roscore:

roscore

you will see this following respone in terminal

started roslaunch server http://ubuntu:35475/

docs.title: Terminal 2
docs.text:
in this terminal you will run urg_node that we already installed before. if you miss that step, make sure to visit this

before we run urg_node, we will run sourcing the setup.bash like Terminal 1 did in the first two step.

note

make sure you are in your catkin workspace

and now we just need to run the urg_node command using:

rosrun urg_node urg_node _ip_address:=192.168.0.10

important

change the IP Address value if you changed the IP Address of LIDAR.

you will see the following response in terminal

[ INFO] [1741755421.699077572]: Connected to network device with intensity and ID: B1906953
[ INFO] [1741755421.725008825]: waitForService: Service [/diagnostics_agg/add_diagnostics] has not been advertised, waiting...
[ INFO] [1741755421.735644579]: Streaming data.

now the lidar is scanning.

docs.title: Setting up workspace
docs.text: you need to seting up workspace correcttly in order to run lidar perfectly

docs.title: Setup catkin workspace
docs.text: this is where you will write your code for Hokuyo UST-10LX LIDAR

docs.title: Create catkin directory
docs.text:
make a directory where you want your workspace to be

mkdir -p  ~/{your_directory}/catkin_ws
cd ~/{your_directory}/catkin_ws

important

changes the your_directory into your desired directory and also the directory catkin_ws is not an absolute directory name , you can change it.

docs.title: Catkin make command
docs.text:
this step will generate our catkin workspace.

in your catkin_ws directory run this following command:

catkin_make

catkin will generate a new workspace, and you will see this following directory on your catkin_ws directory

> ls
src/ devel/ build/

now you ready to operate Hokuyo UST-10LX LIDAR

docs.title: Step by Step
docs.text: here is must followed step by step to make sure your LIDAR will working smoothly

docs.title: Installing Required ROS Packages
docs.text: below packages are required ROS Packages to run Hokuyo UST-10LX LIDAR.

docs.title: 1. urg-node
docs.text:
urg-node is required to make communication between Hokuyo UST-10LX and our peripheral

Install urg-node via apt : 

sudo apt instsall ros-noetic-urg-node

docs.title: 2. rviz
docs.text:
rviz is a ROS Packages to visualize the output data from LIDAR.

Install rviz via apt :

sudo apt install rviz

after everything installed, now lets setup our workspace
